Mauro Bacci, «I Ministeriali del Patriarcato di Aquileia», Padua 2003. The inventory of the Archivio Camillo De Franceschi e famiglia, SIASP Trieste. None of these is yet held by this project; all are in print and obtainable.

svetvincenat.heading: Svetvinčenat — a third Carnian household of the name, and this archive had never looked
svetvincenat.lead: This page has followed the family from Agrons to Mione to Moncalvo. There was a third place, forty kilometres south, and four separate scholars have written about it while this archive was looking elsewhere. It came up because a search of the record indexes was rebuilt after being caught out, and Svetvinčenat came back second only to Rijeka.

rows.lab: 1734 — the household book of Svetvinčenat
rows.text: Danijela Doblanović, working the parish registers, isolates the surnames that appear in the «Status animarum» of 1734 in the town of Svetvinčenat itself and not in the surrounding villages: «Većinom je riječ o stanovnicima koji su došli s prostora Karnije… (prezimena De Franceschi, Crosila, Bergamo, Moro, Fiorencis i tako dalje)» — mostly inhabitants who came from the area of Carnia; the surnames De Franceschi, Crosila, Bergamo, Moro, Fiorencis and so on. And she adds what they did: «Krnjeli/Karnjeli su se uglavnom bavili trgovinom» — the Carnians were mainly engaged in trade.

rows.lab: And a second historian says the same
rows.text: Angelo Ciuffardi, on eighteenth-century Svetvinčenat: about three hundred and thirty inhabitants, «većinom venetskog ili karnijskog podrijetla» — mostly of Venetian or Carnian origin — and his list from the notarial records runs «Monti, Galante, Comin, Vorano, Volpi, Marani, Vernier, Manzin, Fiorencis, Zanetin, Lupieri, Defranceschi, Fabris, Bortolini, Manzoni, Bergamo, Zuliani». Lupieri and Fiorencis are Val di Gorto surnames. It is the same cohort, named twice by different scholars from different sources.

rows.lab: 1820 — and they were burghers, not peasants
rows.text: The house-owner protocol of the Franciscan cadastre for Svetvinčenat, transcribed by Altić and Kliman Grabar, gives three of the town's seventy-three houses to this surname: «Antonio de Franceschi (14/4)», «Pietro Antonio de Franceschi (29/51)» and «casa Antonio de Franceschi (30)». The authors note that «casa» marks the more important houses of the more prominent families. And the status column: only Grimani is a Ritter, a nobleman; a named group including de Franceschi is marked «Burgeri», citizens; and the majority are «Bauer», peasants.

rows.lab: Which is what Kandler and Brhan already said
rows.text: Pietro Kandler's mid-nineteenth-century list of the Carnian-origin families of Sanvincenti, printed by Brhan, has «Lupieri, Fiorencis, Defranceschi, Fabris, Vernier, Gonano, Vorano, Zuliani, Crosilla, Sandri, Corva, Spinotti e altre». And Brhan's own eighteenth-century notarial material gives «D.no Vittorio De Franceschi» among the landed proprietors, and a «Gasparo De Franceschi, carnico pure lui» — himself a Carnian — whose widow Maria Zanco left his capital, should their children die, to his kinswomen Pasqua and Antonia De Franceschi.

rows.lab: So: not one Carnian settlement in Istria, but at least three
rows.text: Gologorica in the Habsburg county of Pazin, where a Gian Battista is «il vecchio stipite» dead in November 1686 and where his descendant cut ANNO · DOMNI · 1711 over the door. Gračišće — Gallignana — the next parish east, where the same stock is in the baptism book by 1679 and where the direct line of this archive is still holding houses 5 and 19 into the nineteenth century: Joannes Baptista the farmer born 1787, Antonius the «lapidarius» born 1825, Josephus born 1863. And Svetvinčenat, over the border in Venetian Istria — a different state, a different landlord, a different set of parish books — with a household of the name established by 1734 and still holding three houses in 1820. Gologorica and Gračišće are four kilometres apart and share their people; Svetvinčenat is forty kilometres south and shares only the valley it came from. Whether that is one family arriving twice or two households out of the same Carnian valleys taking different roads is not answerable from anything this archive holds. What can be said is that the second one was there, that it was Carnian, that it traded rather than farmed, and that it ranked as citizens in a village of peasants.

rows.lab: And by 1945 it was one household
rows.text: The Yugoslav cadastre of 1945 counts a single «De Franceschi» family at Svetvinčenat. The «Stanza De Franceschi» farmstead that Brhan names among the holdings around the castle is gone from the map: the surviving stancija names are Grimani's and Stancovich's. Two hundred years, three houses, and then one.

rows.lab: And then the name kept going
rows.text: None of these three places is where the family is now. From Gračišće the direct line went down to Crikvenica on the Kvarner coast, and from there — by way of a labour camp at Pfullingen and a displaced-persons office — to Zimbabwe and to South Africa and to Australia. The wider surname went further and earlier: the largest cluster of all is in Rio Grande do Sul in Brazil from the 1880s, with names at Arroio do Tigre, Candelária and Porto Alegre; there is a thinner Argentine one from the same decade; the United States indexes carry forty-nine graves and a hundred and twenty-seven vital records, among them Basilio and Dario Defranceschi «born 26 September 1937 in GALLIGNANA, Austria» — the only American entry so far that names Gračišće outright. Australia holds fifteen graves and begins in 1949, with the post-war displacements. Which is the ordinary shape of it: a mountain valley empties into a province, the province empties into a coast, and the coast empties into four continents inside three generations.
rows.linktext: The country-by-country reckoning is on the Diaspora page

rows.lab: And they had a farmstead named after them
rows.text: Brhan, listing the buildings of the Comune censuario di Sanvincenti in the **Catasto franceschino of 1820**, notes that of the seventy-three the last five by number were the *stanzie* just outside the town — and that by 1820 some were **no longer in Carnian hands, «come la Stanzia Spinotti o la Stanzia De Franceschi»**. So there was a **Stanzia De Franceschi at Svetvinčenat**: a named farmstead, on the cadastral map, that the family had held and had already lost by the time the Austrians measured it. That is a great deal more than a scatter of register entries, and it is the strongest reason yet to treat this cluster as a Carnian household of substance rather than a coincidence of surname.

rows.lab: A note for the southern lane
rows.text: The same paper puts **Defranceschi among the Carnian families scattered through the contrade of Barbana** — Agostinis, Cleva, Defranceschi, Valle, Fornasar, Zuliani, Bordon, Ventin. And it quotes the Austrian report of **1816** on Barban: «*vi sono tre tessitori, due fabbri, due sarti e quattro muratori, tutti però foresti che annualmente si portano nella loro patria in Carnia*» — three weavers, two smiths, two tailors and four masons, all of them outsiders who go home to Carnia every year. **This archive's fourth line has Barban in it**, and has always read it as part of the southern-Istrian cluster out of Pula. It may instead be Carnian and seasonal. Left as a flag on the Lines page rather than a rearrangement.

rows.lab: And the two towns describe the same business
rows.text:
Doblanović's paper on the seasonality of conception at Svetvinčenat, read in full in September 2026, adds a detail her better-known sentence does not. The Carnian surnames — **De Franceschi, Crosila, Bergamo, Moro, Fiorencis** — appear in the Status animarum of 1734 **only inside the *castello*, and not in the villages and *stancije* around it**. They were town people. And she says what they did: «**Krnjeli/Karnjeli su se uglavnom bavili trgovinom**» — the Carnians were mainly in trade — and specifically that their work as «**prekupci i preprodavači**», **buyers-up and resellers**, was busiest when there was most produce to buy.

Set that beside the finding aid of this family's own archive at Rijeka, which describes the Gologorica house growing rich through the eighteenth century by «**lending money and buying up debts**» as far as Kastav, Mošćenice, Labin and Carniola. **Two scholars, two towns forty kilometres apart, one trade.** The Carnians who came to Istria were not labourers who prospered; they were the people who bought the crop and lent against it.

svetvincenat.next: Where to look. The Svetvinčenat parish registers and the Status animarum of 1732 and 1734 are in the state archive at Pazin; the estate papers are in the Grimani archive at Venice and in DAPA's «Feudalna uprava Svetvinčenat». And Danijela Doblanović's «Žrvanj života. Stanovništvo Savičente od početka 17. do početka 19. stoljeća» (Zagreb 2017) is built directly on those registers — it is not open access anywhere, and it is where Gasparo, Vittorio, Pasqua and Antonia will be found.
svetvincenat.source_sv: Danijela Doblanović, «Sezonska kretanja začeća/rođenja župe Svetvinčenat u 18. stoljeću», Povijesni prilozi 43 (2012), pp. 217–233; Angelo Ciuffardi, «Svetvinčenat: kratka povijest», Vjesnik istarskog arhiva 6–7 (1996–97), pp. 67–80; Mirela Slukan Altić and Aldo Kliman Grabar, «Na kunfinu: povijest prostornoga razvoja Svetvinčenta», Histria 10 (2020), pp. 11–32; Dean Brhan (2004) for Kandler's list and the notarial material. All open access on Hrčak and at crsrv.org, read September 2026.

twobranches.heading: And a claim this archive has to contest
twobranches.lead: Petar Puhmajer's monograph on the Seget house, which this site already uses and admires, states in one sentence that the Gologorica and the Seget families are two branches of one family. This archive believes that is wrong, and the reasons are worth setting out, because the same assumption will be made again by anyone who meets the surname twice.
twobranches.quote: Venieri su prodali Seget 1720. obitelji de Franceschi koja je u Istru došla izbjegavši s Krete nakon Kandijskog rata 1669. godine. … Postojale su dvije grane obitelji u Istri, jedna sa sjedištem u Gologorici, a druga u Umagu i Segetu.
twobranches.en: The Venier sold Seget in 1720 to the de Franceschi family, which had come to Istria having fled from Crete after the Cretan War of 1669. … There were two branches of the family in Istria, one seated at Gologorica, the other at Umag and Seget.

rows.lab: The two accounts of origin are incompatible
rows.text: The Seget family is said by its own tradition to have come from Crete after 1669, by way of Rome. The Gologorica family is recorded at Moncalvo from 1661 — eight years before the fall of Candia — and every scholar who has looked at where it came from says Carnia. Those are not two branches of one story. They are two stories.

rows.lab: A specialist says so explicitly
rows.text: Dean Brhan, writing on the Carnian migration and listing the families it brought: «I De Franceschi di Moncalvo erano originari di Agrons e i loro consanguinei abitavano nelle villa di Mione. Non sono da confondere con i numerosi De Franceschi carnici presenti in Istria in altre località o con i De Franceschi di Umago che hanno un origine completamente diversa» — not to be confused with the De Franceschi of Umago, who have a completely different origin. He says it unprompted, in a study that has no interest in the question.

rows.lab: The carvings do not match
rows.text: Gologorica bears a cross crossed by two arrows above a pomegranate, under a plumed helm — the blazon Carlo described from memory in 1876, and the one cut on the house, on both tomb tablets and on the urn. The Umag ironwork of 1890 bears a lion rampant and a five-pointed star under a coronet, and the Seget pediment a beast on a lined field. Two families, two coats.

rows.lab: And the archives are two fonds
rows.text: The state archive at Rijeka holds «Obitelj de Franceschi iz Šegeta» as a discrete named fond. The Zagreb librarians who catalogued the Gologorica papers state that in the Rijeka boxes «došlo do spajanja fondova dviju obitelji De Franceschi koje zajedno nemaju ništa osim istarskog zavičaja i prezimena» — the fonds of two De Franceschi families were merged, families which have nothing in common but an Istrian homeland and a surname. The archivists who handled the papers reached the same conclusion this archive has.

rows.lab: Said fairly
rows.text: Puhmajer's book is a careful architectural study and this site relies on it for Seget. The two-branch sentence is one line, unfootnoted, resting on a gazetteer, in a work about a building; and the word Carnia never appears in it. It is the kind of thing anyone writes when a surname turns up twice in one province. This archive has published both families for months and kept them apart, and now has three independent reasons to go on doing so.

rows.lab: And there is a way to settle it, written by Camillo himself
rows.text: Camillo De Franceschi — Carlo's son, of the Gologorica family — published «Il Consiglio nobile di Parenzo e i profughi di Creta» in the «Atti e memorie della Società istriana di archeologia e storia patria», new series volume 2, in 1952. It is a study of exactly the migration the Seget family's tradition claims: the refugees who came out of Crete when Candia fell in 1669, and how the noble council of Poreč received them. If a De Franceschi family arrived from Crete and settled in Venetian Istria, that paper is where it would be named — and the man who wrote it was a professional archivist who knew his own family's papers better than anyone alive. This archive has not read it. It is not digitised, and no library within reach holds the 1952 volume. It is now the first item on the acquisition list, because it is the single document most likely to decide the question either way.

twobranches.source_two: Petar Puhmajer, «Stancija de Franceschi u Segetu kod Umaga», Mala biblioteka Godišnjaka zaštite spomenika kulture Hrvatske 20 (Zagreb 2019), section 2.2, p. 9 — open access at min-kulture.gov.hr and held in this project's library. Against it: Brhan (2004); the carvings photographed by the family in 2026; and Marin, Jurišić and Matijaca, Arhivski vjesnik 67 (2024).

brhan3.heading: Three more papers by the one scholar who has actually studied this migration
brhan3.lead: This archive has leaned on Dean Brhan's «In partibus Carsi et Istriae» for a year. A full-text sweep of the whole open-access run of the Centro di ricerche storiche at Rovinj — 1,303 articles, every one downloaded and read by machine — turned up three more of his papers that this project had never seen. They name this family four times, and one of the notes is the plainest statement about it that any specialist has published.

rows.lab: Brhan's own verdict, in a footnote
rows.text: «Un caso a parte era sicuramente la famiglia De Franceschi di Moncalvo-Gologoriza, un villaggio del comune di Cerreto vicino a Pisino. La famiglia, presente in Istria dal 1650 circa, originaria di Mione, si era distinta nella zona come possidente… Rimane non chiaro il loro legame con le radici carniche, che erano piuttosto deboli se paragonate con altre famiglie presenti sul suolo istriano. In un contesto compattamente croato i de Franceschi, che erano una delle pochissime famiglie carniche del paese, erano stati i promotori dell'italianità dell'ex Contea di Pisino e dell'Istria.»

rows.lab: In English, and it is not entirely a compliment
rows.text: A case apart was certainly the De Franceschi family of Moncalvo–Gologorica, a village of the commune of Cerreto near Pazin. The family, present in Istria from about 1650, originating from Mione, had distinguished itself in the area as a landholding family… Their link with their Carnian roots remains unclear, and was rather weak compared with other families present on Istrian soil. In a compactly Croatian setting the de Franceschi, who were one of the very few Carnian families of the village, had been the promoters of the Italian-ness of the former County of Pazin and of Istria. — Two dates in one sentence: present from about 1650, originating from Mione. And a judgement this archive is not going to soften: the specialist thinks they kept the Carnian origin more thinly than their neighbours did, and turned into the local standard-bearers of an Italian identity in a Croatian village.

rows.lab: And the family is named at Gračišće, in the cadastre
rows.text: Listing, village by village, the Carnian households that show in the Franciscan cadastre of 1820: «Nel vicino borgo di Lindaro c'erano Giuseppe Picot, Giovanni Pascoli, Matteo, Antonio e Francesco Gortan… A Gallignana le seguenti famiglie; Gortan, De Franceschi, Festa, Picot, Baldè; mentre a Pedena i Rovis e i Comisso.» De Franceschi at Gallignana, counted as Carnian, in 1820 — which is the village of houses 5 and 19 and the year the farmer Joannes Baptista of house 5 was thirty-three.

rows.lab: Tombs in the church at Svetvinčenat
rows.text: «Durante il XVIII secolo due Lupieri, Matteo e GioBatta, erano stati sepolti nella chiesa matrice di questo borgo istriano. Nello stesso luogo si trovano le tombe di numerose famiglie carniche come i Crosilla, i Gherssan, i Misdaris, i De Franceschi, i Mirai, i Merlin e i Zambiasio.» De Franceschi tombs inside the parish church of Svetvinčenat, among the Carnian families. Burial in the matrice is not where the poor go.

rows.lab: A boy of nineteen, in another Carnian's house
rows.text: From the household lists of Svetvinčenat: «Il Domino Giobatta Lupieri Cargnello di anni 33 era il giudice della comunità per quell'anno e viveva insieme al garzone Piero Defranceschi, un giovane di 19 anni.» Giobatta Lupieri, Carnian, thirty-three, judge of the community that year — and living in his house, Piero Defranceschi, a lad of nineteen, his «garzone»: apprentice, shop-boy, servant. The Carnians of Svetvinčenat took each other's sons in.

rows.lab: And two more names for the index
rows.text: «Prencis Zuane da Dignano (cognato di Sebastiano de Franceschi e di Micoli)» — Zuane Prencis of Dignano, brother-in-law of Sebastiano de Franceschi. And at Buzet: the weaver Giobatta Zanier called «Zuel», born at Mione in 1790, «si era accasato in Istria insieme alla moglie Maria De Franceschi» — settled in Istria with his wife Maria De Franceschi, and bought the Micoli Toscano property at Pinguente in 1825. A De Franceschi woman of the Mione stock, marrying another Mione weaver, and the pair of them going down together.

brhan3.source_b3: Dean Brhan, «Stare cum loco et foco. L'emigrazione verso l'Istria dalla Carnia», Atti CRS 46 (2016), pp. 91–136; «Absentati in histrianas partes. L'emigrazione della borghesia di montagna del Canale di Gorto in Istria», Atti CRS 47 (2017), pp. 169–211, the family at note 74; «La corrispondenza istriana della famiglia Lupieri», Quaderni CRS 29 (2018), pp. 355–378. All three open access at crsrv.org, downloaded and read September 2026, and held in this project's source library.

fieldplates.heading: And the family went and stood in it
fieldplates.lead: This page has argued the Carnian origin from documents for a year — Carlo's letter to Kobler, the headmen's return of 1679, Brhan, Bertoša, Matejčić. In 2026 the family drove to the Val Degano and photographed the ground. Ninety-four frames from Ovaro, Mione, Muina and Agrons. What they show is that the argument was not about a lost people.

rows.lab: The byname is real, and it is on a gravestone
rows.text: «SEBASTIANO SORAVITO DE FRANCESCHI ✻1889 ✝1958», with «ANNA CROSILLA VED. SORAVITO DE FRANCESCHI ✻1900 ✝1990» beneath him. This archive first met «Soravito De Franceschi» in David's family tree and did not know what to make of it. It is a Carnian house-name, it is cut in stone at Ovaro, and the woman beside him is a **Crosilla** — one of the surnames Kandler and Brhan both list among the Carnian families that went to Svetvinčenat.

rows.lab: And the name is not a memory there
rows.text: «DE FRANCESCHI UGO, 24.11.1930 – 4.6.2020.» A photograph behind glass, a lamp burning in front of it. Another stone in the same ground is dated 2022. This site has published that the surname is down to about ten people in Croatia; in the valley it came from, it was being buried five years ago.

rows.lab: Two of them on the war memorial
rows.text: «DE FRANCESCHI VITTORIO» and «DE FRANCESCHI ISIDORO», among the fallen and the missing of 1940–45, with Micoli, Spinotti, Stefani, Lorenzini and Fabris beside them — the same dozen surnames that run through every document in these villages and through the Carnian settlements in Istria.

rows.lab: Under the tower the 1679 list was drawn up beneath
rows.text: The Romanesque campanile of **Santa Maria di Gorto** over the graves. This is the mother church of the Val Degano, and its two parishes — Ovaro and Luincis — are the ones whose headmen made the return of 1679 that names «Zuane De Franceschi con un suo fiolo, Zuane d'Erman: questi tre nell'Istria, luogo imperiale». The men who wrote that list are buried under this tower.

fieldplates.source_fp: Photographed by the family in Carnia, 2026 — ninety-four frames from Ovaro, Mione, Muina and Agrons. Inscriptions transcribed from the images; living people are excluded from this archive and their frames are not published.

gortostones.heading: Thirty stones, photographed and now published
gortostones.lead: The prose above was written from what the family reported. The frames themselves had never been put on this site. Here are eighteen of them, plated at last — and read together they say two things the individual inscriptions do not.

rows.lab: The names they married are the names that went to Istria
rows.text:
Read the stones as a list of in-laws and something jumps out. A De Franceschi at Gorto married a **Soravito**, a **Pustetto**, a **Rovis**, a **Giorgis**, a **Fiorencis**, a **Corva**, a **Crosilla**, a **Misdariis**, a **Dell'Oste**, a **Mirai**, an **Adami**, a **Cecconi**.

**Rovis** are the Carnian family of Gimino in Istria, out of Agrons. **Giorgis** are the Carnian family of San Pietro in Selve, out of Mione. **Fiorencis** and **Crosilla** are two of the four surnames the household book of Svetvinčenat names in 1734 as «inhabitants who came from the area of Carnia», alongside De Franceschi itself. **Corva** appear in the Sanvincenti court papers. **Spinotti**, on the war memorial three names above ours, are the one Carnian house that got Venetian noble recognition, and they settled at Grisignana.

So this graveyard is not simply where the family came from. **It is a directory of the exact set of families that colonised Istria** — and they married each other at home as consistently as they did abroad. The literature calls that a marriage strategy for holding property together. The stones are what it looks like.

rows.lab: And one stone runs the other way
rows.text:
A tablet on the cemetery wall: «**INS. MARIO FURLANI · ALBONA 1912 · OVARO 1978**». A schoolmaster, *insegnante*, **born at Albona — Labin, in Istria — in 1912, and dead at Ovaro in 1978**.

Everything on this page describes a road out of Carnia into Istria. This is a man who came back up it, and lies in the valley his family had left. **Labin is also where the surname is first indexed anywhere in Istria** — Aloÿsius Defranceschi, 1615. Furlani is not our name and nothing joins him to this family. He is here because the whole argument of this page is that the two countries were one world, and a stone that says *born Albona, died Ovaro* proves it in five words.

rows.lab: The name is not historical here
rows.text: **De Franceschi Anna, born 22 February 1925, died 5 October 2022.** The most recent burial of the surname in the churchyard, four years ago, with fresh flowers on it. Whatever happened to the Istrian branches, in the Val Degano the name is still being cut into stone.

rows.lab: Two brothers, and the war that took them
rows.text: The Pustetto stone carries six people under one roof of marble, each with a porcelain portrait: **Pustetto Francesco 1891–1978** and **De Franceschi Eufemia 1889–1960**, and then their sons **Augusto 1921–1943** — photographed in uniform, dead in the year of the armistice — and **Giobatta 1922–1945**. Their sister **Maria Maddalena 1926–2015** outlived them by seventy years. This stone has been on the archive's return-visit list for months because the death years were out of frame. They are in frame now.

gortostones.source_gorto: Photographed by the family at the cemetery of the Pieve di Santa Maria di Gorto, Ovaro (Udine), October 2026; ninety-four frames, of which eighteen are plated here. Transcriptions are read from the photographs. The Carnian surnames are identified from Dean Brhan's studies of the Carnia–Istria migration and from Danijela Doblanović on the Svetvinčenat Status animarum of 1734.

mione1806.heading: And the 1806 book, which nobody had opened either
mione1806.grade: doc — read off the page, 14 September 2026; uncertain words marked
mione1806.lead: The four Mione households already on this page come from the birth registers of **1809 and 1810**. The **1806** volume — the first year the Napoleonic registration ran — had not been read. It is three images long and it holds one act.

act.when: Presented Sunday 19 October 1806 at four in the morning; the child born Friday 17 October at half past one
act.who: **Paolo di Pietro de Franceschi**, of this commune, and **Anna, daughter of Pio Batta Berenzi**, his lawful wife, both *di professione Rurale*
act.child: A daughter, **Mariana** *(the given name is the least certain word on the page)*
act.brought: Brought by the **midwife**, *Maddalena Urban*, aged fifty-nine, who **could not write** and made her mark
act.witnesses: **Pietro q. Giacomo Bulfon of Regolato**, shopkeeper; **Matteo di Giacomo Berenzi** of this commune, *fa legname* — a timber man
act.signed: **Pietro Bulfon**, Deputato, aged fifty · **Filippo di Zuane Prencis**, aged forty · **Giovanni Micoli**, Secretary and Officer of the Civil State
act.ref: Archivio di Stato di Udine · Stato civile napoleonico · Mione · 1806 · Nati · segnatura 12950 · Antenati ark an_ua667570, image 3 of 3

why.lab: It is a fifth household, and it has a generation the others do not
why.text: The four already published are Osvaldo × Appolonia Galante at Muina, Francesco × Margherita Gortan at Mione, Osvaldo × Cattarina Brencis at Mione, and Pasqua married into the Luchin. **Paolo di Pietro is none of them** — and he carries his father's name with him. **Pietro de Franceschi of Mione** stands behind this act without appearing in it, which is one generation further back than anything the 1809 and 1810 books gave.

why.lab: And a second De Franceschi signs it
why.text:
The midwife could not write, so another man signed for her: **Osvaldo de Franceschi, son of the late Osvaldo**, *«d'anni diciannove circa»* — about nineteen.

This archive already has an **Osvaldo De Franceschi, aged 26, a carpenter at Mione in 1810**. Nineteen in 1806 and twenty-six in 1810 are **three years apart and cannot both be right**, so they are either the same man with a loosely-given age or two men of one name. **What is certain either way is the father: an older Osvaldo, dead before October 1806.** The archive had no generation above its two Osvaldos until now.

why.lab: What it does not do
why.text: It does not reach Zuane of 1679, and nothing here joins Mione to Istria. **The 1806 book is one act long.** The weight of this village sits in the *marriage allegati* — twenty-eight of them survive for Ovaro — because those attach the parties' own birth and death certificates and reach back before the registers begin.

mione1809.heading: The allegati deliver what this page said they would
mione1809.grade: doc for the two extracts, read off the page at high magnification on 14 September 2026 · inf for the pairing of them, which is taken from the file's own bundling and not from a marriage act
mione1809.lead: Two paragraphs above, this page said that a single De Franceschi marriage at Mione between 1806 and 1815 «would reach back into the middle of the eighteenth century». **It does.** The first bundle of the *Mione, Matrimoni allegati* for **1809** is two baptismal extracts, written out by the same parish priest ten days apart, and one of them is this family's.

act.when: Certified at Luincis on 4 February 1809, and seen by the civil officer Valentino Lupieri for the Comune di Mione
act.who: **«Orsola figlia legittima e naturale di Pietro quondam Matteo De Franceschi di Mione e di Maddalena sua moglie»**
act.child: Born **11 April 1768** — *«essa è venuta alla luce li 11 del mese d'Aprile nell'anno 1768, come appare dai pubblici registri dei Battezzati»*
act.brought: The other extract in the bundle: **«Giovanni = Pietro = Antonio figlio legittimo e naturale di Pietro cramaro del villaggio di Mione»**, born 28 April **1752**, certified 10 February 1809 — the groom. *«Cramaro» is not his surname but his father's trade.* The marriage act names the family **ERMAN**.
act.witnesses: Both written by **D. Giovanni Battista Dazio**, parish priest of the **Pieve Matrice del Canal di Gorto, a parte Luincis**
act.signed: Docketed by the file's own clerk as **«Matrimonj N. 1 · Mione · 1809»**
act.ref: Archivio di Stato di Udine · Stato civile napoleonico · Mione · Matrimoni, allegati · 1809 · Antenati ark an_ua667530, images 2 and 3 of 39

why.lab: It is a generation above the deepest name on this page
why.text:
The 1806 act gave **Pietro de Franceschi of Mione**, who stood behind his son Paolo's name without appearing in the register himself. That was the furthest back the village went.

This extract names **Pietro's own father**. *«Pietro quondam Matteo»* — **Matteo De Franceschi of Mione**, dead before February 1809, and the father of a man whose daughter was born in **1768**. A man whose granddaughter was born in 1768 belongs to a generation born around **1700 to 1720** — which is within living memory of the Zuane De Franceschi who left this valley for Istria in **1679**.

why.lab: And she is the earliest-born De Franceschi of Mione with a day and a month
why.text:
**Orsola, 11 April 1768.** Every other Mione De Franceschi in this archive is dated from the Napoleonic registers, which begin in 1806. She is dated from the **baptismal book of the Pieve di Gorto**, thirty-eight years earlier, by the priest who was reading it.

She was **forty** when these papers were drawn. Her intended was **fifty**.

why.lab: A daughter marrying out — and the name she married into
why.text:
Orsola married **Giovanni Pietro Erman**, and after 1809 she is an Erman in every record that mentions her. This is exactly how the twenty-six married-out daughters on this archive's open list disappear.

**And the name she married into is the other name in the 1679 list.** That list of village headmen recorded at Mione: *«Zuane De Franceschi con un suo fiolo, **Zuane d'Erman**: questi tre nell'Istria, luogo imperiale»* — a De Franceschi, his son, and an **Erman**, all three working in Istria.

**A hundred and thirty years later the two families are still marrying each other in the same village** — and the groom's own mother was **Maddalena née de Franceschi**, so 1809 is at least the second crossing between them.

why.lab: What is documented and what is not
why.text: **All of it is now documented.** When this section was first written the pairing of the two extracts was graded *inferred*, because the marriage act sat in a different volume and had not been read. **It has now been read**, and it confirms the pairing — while correcting the groom's surname and his birth year. See the act itself below, and the correction.

mione1811.heading: And in the 1811 file, a priest of the name
mione1811.grade: doc — Latin extract read at high magnification, 14 September 2026; the forename abbreviated in the original as «Franc.o Ant.o» and expanded here
mione1811.lead: The 1811 allegati hold no De Franceschi marriage. They hold something else. Buried in the papers of a bride called Anna Maria Giorgi is a certified copy of **her own baptism of 1785**, and the priest who performed it carries this surname.

act.when: Baptism **20 February 1785**; the extract certified at **Luincis, 20 June 1811**, from the register of the Pieve
act.who: **«hodie de mea licentia a R. D. Franc.o Ant.o Deffranceschi de Mione … solemniter fuit baptizata»** — today, by my licence, by the Reverend Father **Francesco Antonio Deffranceschi of Mione**, she was solemnly baptised
act.child: **Anna Maria**, lawful daughter of **Giovanni Domenico, son of the late Giovanni Battista Giorgi «de Nave»**, of Mione, and **Lucia** his wife — born the evening before, after sunset
act.witnesses: In the parish church of the Pieve, by licence of the parish priest, who wrote the entry in the first person
act.signed: Copied out in 1811 because the child of 1785 was marrying
act.ref: Archivio di Stato di Udine · Stato civile napoleonico · Mione · Matrimoni, allegati · 1811 · Antenati ark an_ua667534, image 23 of 74

why.lab: The first cleric of this surname this archive has found in Carnia
why.text:
He is styled **«de Mione»** — of the village, not merely serving it — and he is a **Reverendus Dominus** acting with the parish priest's licence in the mother church of the whole valley.

This archive already holds **Mattia Defranceschi, parish priest of Gologorica in Istria**, named in the diocesan visitation of **1788**. Two priests of one surname, **three years apart**: one in the Carnian valley this family came from, one in the Istrian parish it went to.

**No link is claimed between them.** What is worth saying is that this is not an isolated oddity — the Istrian encyclopedia entry already transcribed on this page lists a string of De Franceschi clerics who kept working *in Carnia* long after the crossing: «Filippo, son of Gian Battista, parish priest at Previs; Gian Matteo, son of Gian Pietro, parish priest at Moncalvo, canon of the cathedral of Pedena». **A De Franceschi priest at Mione in 1785 is exactly what that list predicts.**

why.lab: How a document from 1785 ends up in a file from 1811
why.text:
It is the ordinary machinery of the Napoleonic marriage, and it is why these files matter. To marry, the bride had to produce her baptism. The parish priest copied it out of the register and certified the copy, and the copy was filed with the marriage.

So **the allegati carry the parish registers forward into the state archive**. The 1785 entry survives here whatever became of the book it was copied from — and it survives in a volume catalogued under 1811.

why.lab: What the rest of the year holds
why.text: Seventy-four pages, and no marriage of this family in them. The names that pass through are **Gortan, Zorzi, Bassi, Micoli, Bilbiani, Vernier, Crosilla, Sortiza, Varnier, Gaier of Forni Avoltri**, and a bride from **Cesclans**. That is a clean negative for 1811, and it is recorded as one.

mione1812.heading: 1812, and a hamlet with a name
mione1812.grade: doc for the godparent entry, read at high magnification 14 September 2026 · inf for the identification with the elder Osvaldo
mione1812.lead: No De Franceschi married at Mione in 1812 either. But the brides and grooms of 1812 had to produce baptisms going back to the 1780s, and **a surname turns up in a register long before it turns up in a marriage** — standing at the font.

act.when: Baptism **10 January 1789**; extract certified at **Luincis, 28 June 1812**
act.who: **«ex sacro fonte suscepta fuit a D. Osvaldo DeFranceschi de Nave Mionensis»** — lifted from the sacred font by **Don Osvaldo DeFranceschi of Nave, of Mione**
act.child: **Anna Maria**, lawful daughter of **Pietro Pellis of Cella** and Sabbata his wife, baptised in danger of death the evening she was born
act.brought: The other godparent: **Maria, wife of Giuseppe Pellis of Cella**
act.witnesses: Also in this file: the death extracts of **Nicolò quondam Antonio Corva of Muina**, died 11 August 1808, and of **Jacoba his wife**, died 6 February 1801 — both styled *«de Nave»*
act.signed: Filed because a child of 1789 was marrying in 1812
act.ref: Archivio di Stato di Udine · Stato civile napoleonico · Mione · Matrimoni, allegati · 1812 · Antenati ark an_ua667535, image 30 of 54

why.lab: It is probably the elder Osvaldo, seen alive
why.text:
The 1806 birth act gave a young **«Osvaldo de Franceschi, son of the late Osvaldo»**, and this page said of it: *«What is certain either way is the father: an older Osvaldo, dead before October 1806.»* He was a name with no sighting.

A man standing godfather in **January 1789** is an adult. An adult in 1789 who is dead by 1806 is exactly the shape of that father. **The identification is inferred, not documented** — no document joins the two — but it is the only Osvaldo of this surname the village is known to have had in that generation, and he is here with the honorific **«D.»**, *Dominus*, which the priest did not give to everybody on the page.

why.lab: Nave
why.text:
He is **«de Nave»** — of Nave, a named place, not of Mione at large. Until today this archive had never recorded the name.

It now has it repeatedly from these files: **Giorgi «de Nave» Mionensis** (1785), **Corva «de Nave»** (1785 and 1801), this **De Franceschi «de Nave»** (1789), **«Dominus Joannes Micoli-Toscano de Nave Mionensis»** (1794) — and, in the Lenzone file, **Fiorenzi «de Nave» Luincis** (1778).

**That last one matters, because it means Nave is not simply a corner of Mione.** The clerks attach it to Mione and to Luincis alike, which makes it a small locality in the Ovaro cluster shared between the two — not a sub-division of either. This archive first wrote «a hamlet of Mione» and has corrected it.

What survives the correction is the important part: **the same tiny place holds a De Franceschi household and the Micoli Toscano**, whose palace archive keeps the 1679 Gorto contracts naming the Erman who travelled to Istria with Zuane De Franceschi. Not merely the same village — the same handful of houses.

why.lab: What this changes about how to read these files
why.text:
Four years of allegati have now produced **one marriage** of this family and **two sightings that are not marriages** — a priest in 1785, a godfather in 1789.

That is the lesson. The allegati are not an index of who married; they are **a seam of certified extracts copied out of parish registers that no longer have to survive**, and the surname appears in them as godparent, as celebrant, as neighbour. **Reading them only for the couple would have missed both.**

why.lab: The rest of 1812
why.text: Fifty-four pages. The names are **Brovedan, Zoran, Spinotti, Fadri, Pellis, Stefani, Corva, Pedri, Martin, Brugia, Manetti, De Stephano, Capedari, Drossi, Cleva**, with **Brenci, Lupieri, Micoli, Novi** and **Sallenati of Sutrio** as godparents and witnesses. No De Franceschi marriage.

mionedone.heading: All twelve Mione files, and what the whole run came to
mionedone.lead: Mione's marriage allegati run from **1806 to 1815** in twelve volumes — not the two this archive first counted. All twelve have now been read. **Four are not allegati at all**: they are one-sheet covering letters from the Comune to the court at Udine and Passariano, signed by the civil officers **Valentino Lupieri** and **Giacomo Micoli**. The other eight hold about **fifty marriages in 420 pages**.
rows: Filed with Muina and the other villages; the Muina file of 1806–07 holds Corva × Fabris and Micoli, and no De Franceschi.
**Osvaldo de Franceschi × Appolonia Galante**, bundle number one of eleven. The widow's consent, the two baptismal extracts, and the death of Antonio bracketed to fourteen weeks.
**Orsola De Franceschi, «figlia di Pietro quondam Matteo»**, born 11 April 1768 — the generation above the deepest name the village had. Bundled with Giovanni Pietro Antonio Cramaro.
Nothing. Lorenzin × Urai, Larese × Zanier, Fachin × Stefani, Masin × Brovedan, and the Colledan and Desanutti papers.
No marriage — but a baptism of 1785 performed by **R. D. Francesco Antonio Deffranceschi de Mione**, priest.
No marriage — but **D. Osvaldo DeFranceschi de Nave Mionensis** standing godfather in 1789.
Nothing of the surname. Della Vedova, Clevo, Crisilla, Erman, Micoli Toscano, Jacotti, Sortan, Gortan, Nigris, Plozzi, Machin.
Nothing. Goin, Micoli, Odorico Micoli, Della Pietra, Marcuzzi, Urban, Rubin — and the **Paludi of Verona**, resident at Mione, two of whom die here in 1801 and 1805.
Nothing. Novis of Agrons, Lupieri of Liariis, Brenci, Toriano de Nave, Disopra, Gusset, De Quas, Miudaris.

close.lab: One marriage, two sightings, one new generation
close.text:
That is the whole yield of 420 pages, and it is worth being precise about it. **One marriage of this family in ten years** — and the family was not large. **Two appearances that are not marriages at all** — a priest and a godfather — which only a page-by-page reading could have found. And **one new generation**, Matteo, reached not through a De Franceschi marriage but through a **daughter's**.

The lesson for the rest of this valley is plain: **read the allegati for the surname wherever it falls**, not for the couple on the docket.

The 1808 papers left an open question: the **notary** wrote the bride's surname **Galante**, the **priest and the docket** wrote **Salante**.

Two documents closed it. A witness to a Mione notarial act of 1813 signs himself, in his own hand and a plain lower-case g, **«pietro galante fui presente testimonio»** — so Galante is a real surname in this village. And the **marriage register itself**, read on 14 September 2026, gives **«Appolonia Galante … figlia di Antonio Galante»**.

**Four hands for Galante, two for Salante, and the register among the four.** This archive has changed the name throughout and logged the correction.

The hamlet **Nave** was unknown to this archive this morning. These files name four households in it: **Giorgi de Nave** (1785), **Corva de Nave** (1785, 1801), **De Franceschi de Nave** (1789) — and **«Dominus Joannes Micoli-Toscano de Nave Mionensis»**, godfather in 1794.

**That is the Micoli Toscano**, whose palace at Mione holds the 1679 Gorto contracts this archive has been trying to reach for months — the ones that name the Erman who travelled to Istria with Zuane De Franceschi. They were not merely in the same village as this family. **They were in the same hamlet.**

close.lab: And one man who went the other way
close.text:
Among the 1815 papers the parish priest swears *«per scienza indubitabile»* that **Valentino, son of the late Giambattista Disopra**, of his parish, *«mancò di vita nel giorno 20 Xbre anno 1797 … nella Istria Superiore»* — died in Upper Istria in December 1797, and that word of it came back to the valley by letter. *(The place-name after it is not legible and the priest's geography that follows is confused, so only the province is reported here.)*

He is nobody's relation here. He is the road itself, certified: **a Carnian who died in Istria, and a home parish that knew.**

The same file carries another kind of death — **Giovanni di Domenico de Stefano**, forty, drowned in the **Degano** on 5 May 1779 *«in conductione lignorum»*, working the timber rafts, his body found the next day. The trade that built this valley, and the river that took him.

istriaroad.heading: Two Istrian marriages, filed in Carnia
istriaroad.lead: The Ovaro allegati are not only about Ovaro. Twice in 1807 the papers for a marriage in this valley were made **in Istria**, and the Istrian officials' certificates came back up the mountain to be bound into a Carnian file. **Neither marriage involves this family.** They are published because this archive has spent years arguing that the road from the Val di Gorto to Istria was open and busy, and here it is, in two documents, with both ends of the paperwork in one folder.
rows: Capodistria, May 1807

In the **Ovaro** file. **«L'Ufficiale dello Stato Civile di Capodistria all'Ufficiale dello Stato Civile d'Ovaro. Capodistria li 28 Maggio 1807»** — certifying that on Sundays **17 and 24 May**, at eleven in the morning, the banns were cried in that city. The consent was taken at Ovaro before the notary **Giacomo Machin quondam Pietro** from **Michiele quondam Domenico Cleva** and his wife **Domenica quondam Cristoffolo Bolfar**; a further act was drawn **at Capodistria itself** on 28 May before a notary of that city, and authenticated by **Giovanni Manzini, Deputato Notariale**.
San Lorenzo, July 1807

In the **Lenzone** file, and it reaches further in. **«Dipartimento d'Istria, Distretto di Capodistria, Cantone di Pirano, Comune di S. Lorenzo, li 16 sedici Luglio mille ottocento e sette»** — the civil officer of **San Lorenzo**, today **Sveti Lovreč**, certifying the two Sunday publications of a promise of marriage, for a couple whose file was kept at Lenzone above Ovaro.

Sveti Lovreč is **inland Istria**, twenty kilometres from Poreč — the same country as **Svetvinčenat**, where this archive found its 1628 baptism.
istriaroad.close:
**What this is worth, stated carefully.** It is not evidence about any De Franceschi. It is evidence about **the route**: that in 1807 a Carnian commune and an Istrian one exchanged marriage paperwork as a matter of routine, in both directions, and that the officials at each end knew how to do it.

The argument this archive makes about **1679** — that a Zuane De Franceschi went from this valley to Istria — has always rested on a contract and an inference. It still does. But the traffic it assumes was real, and these two files are the ordinary administrative residue of it, a hundred and thirty years later.

villagefiles.heading: The other fourteen files, and a clean negative
villagefiles.lead: Beyond Mione, the Comune of Ovaro filed marriage allegati for its other villages. **Fourteen volumes, 296 images**, now read. **There is no De Franceschi in any of them.** That is worth publishing as plainly as a discovery, because it bounds the search: between 1806 and 1815 this family married **once** in the whole Ovaro district, and it married at Muina.

Lenzone 1807
10 images. **Istrian** — see below.

27 images. Missana, Mazzolini, and a baptism of 1785 for a son of **Giovanni Battista Del Missier «de Nave Mion»** — a sixth household in that small place — with **Donna Giovanna, wife of Giovanni Micoli-Toscano**, as godmother.

villagefiles.method: **How these were read, stated plainly.** Every short certificate and every baptismal or death extract was read — those are the documents that name people and parentage, and they are where a surname surfaces. The long notarial consents were read from their opening lines, which name the parties, the village and the notary. **The very long files were not transcribed line by line**, and this archive says so rather than implying a completeness it did not achieve. If the surname is hiding in the middle of a sixty-line consent as a neighbour or a boundary, it is still hiding.
